title: Sharp two-sided heat-kernel estimates for isotropic stable SDEs with uniformly nondegenerate Hölder diffusion and locally Hölder linearly growing drift
source_title: Heat kernel of supercritical nonlocal operators with unbounded drifts
author: Stéphane Menozzi; Xicheng Zhang
difficulty_reason: The cited weak well-posedness theorem supplies a process, not sharp stable-tail density bounds for an unbounded supercritical drift. Sections2–3 construct scale-dependent drift flows, close singular parametrix convolutions and derive the off-diagonal lower estimate by a controlled Lévy-system jump. Section5 then preserves these uniform estimates under coefficient smoothing and drift truncation; the new estimates remain required after the named probabilistic foundations are allowed.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Only Theorem1.1(i), including existence of a jointly spatially continuous transition density, for alpha in(0,2), isotropic symmetric alpha-stable noise, Borel time dependence, matrix diffusion bounded uniformly nondegenerate with spatial gamma-Hölder control, and drift satisfying exactH_beta^b linear-growth/local-beta-Hölder bound with alpha+beta>1 and alpha+gamma>1. Exact finite-time two-sided estimate around the scale-mollified drift flow1.21 retained, not around an arbitrary unregularized deterministic flow. Complete new tube/one-jump Lévy estimate, frozen density, kernel convolution, parametrix construction and bounded/unbounded coefficient approximation read. Existing stable Gaussian-subordination density bounds, known weak well-posedness, Schauder estimates and martingale-problem convergence are cited research foundations. No backward-PDE sign assertion, fractional derivative or logarithmic gradient estimate separately included; no cylindrical/asymmetric noise extrapolation. Lemma2.10 difference estimates explicitly invoke prior established lemmas rather than an absent new nonlocal theorem. Smooth-Hölder mollification preserves ellipticity for sufficiently small epsilon by the displayed uniform Hölder approximation; use only this stated small-epsilon regime. Kernel convolution exponent prerequisites may be met by decreasing the permitted Hölder exponents, an ancillary hypothesis choice within the author conditions, not a new parametrix argument. Change-of-variable determinants carry their standard absolute-Jacobian meaning; source1.4 suppresses those bars while explicitly requiring positive Levy density in1.5.
